## TL;DR

Slice 2 now closes the review loop at the prompt, report parser, API, CLI and task drawer. Reviewers are asked to enumerate bug classes, label findings consistently and close Bugs with the grep summary; the parser ignores that closer. Engineers self-review against the same checklist before handoff. After four completed passes, a human can create a follow-up task from the latest non-blocking suggestions. Review pass history now shows the labeled finding classes and the drawer reports “round N of ~4.” The Move-to-done flow offers a confirmed “Land anyway” action only when a current `needs some work` verdict with no blocking Bugs is the sole failed landing check; the reason is written to task activity and the existing close-out pipeline continues unchanged.

## Work and rationale

The work started from the existing slice 1 implementation (#1080), which already carries the freeze threshold, priority-aware blocking bar and accepted-scope instructions. I kept the slice 2 prompt additions in the same shared prompt locations, with tests in `default-agent-prompts.test.ts`.

The Bugs parser now strips only the exact enumeration closer from the Bugs section, so the required line does not become a finding. Reviewer output also requires a stable `**Class: name**` label for each bug. A shared parser extracts those labels, and the review endpoint includes them alongside each numbered pass. The task drawer adds a finding-classes column to its existing history table, and its progress hint uses the completed review-pass counter rather than the auto-bounce counter.

The follow-up endpoint reads the latest stored report on the server, checks that the configured freeze threshold has completed and that Suggestions is non-empty, then creates a p3 task dependent on the reviewed task. It records the current API user as creator, commits the new task file and refreshes the live index. The UI action appears for a current latest report with suggestions after the freeze, and `repoos review followup <id>` uses the same endpoint. No task is created until a human activates one of these controls. During final audit I corrected a mismatch where the drawer and endpoint used a literal four passes despite the configurable freeze threshold; the review response now carries that threshold and both sides use it.

For “Land anyway,” the drawer first requires its current landability snapshot to show the review verdict as the only failed check and opens a shared confirmation dialog requiring a reason. The server independently repeats eligibility checks against the latest report and gathered landing facts; it rejects missing or overlong reasons, stale or failed reports, any verdict other than `needs some work`, blocking Bugs, and any other failed landing check. It records the reason in task activity, then proceeds through the same close-out action and publication pipeline. Thus the override accepts review risk without skipping landing validation.

Documentation now describes enumeration, class history, follow-up creation and the guarded override. The report references #1076 (foreign task bookkeeping) and #1061 (bookkeeping commits affecting checks) as out of scope.

## Approaches tried

I traced the review report parser and close-out route before adding behavior. I avoided changing the close-out gate itself: instead, the server accepts the override only after `gatherLandable` shows every non-verdict check passing and the verdict check failing specifically because the current review says `needs some work`. The route then carries the reason as part of the existing done request. This keeps normal merge, checks, tests and publish behavior on the same path.

Finding classes are reviewer-authored stable labels rather than guessed from arbitrary prose. The prompt establishes the shape, a shared parser extracts it, and each history row displays the labels for that pass. Older reports without labels remain visible with an em dash rather than assigning inferred classes.

## Challenges and blockers

The required scoped check was not green on its first attempt. RepoOS could not use three remote runners because their link probes fell below the throughput requirement, then ran the local fallback. Build, format, lint, contrast, and the user-docs build passed. The test step reported two unrelated failures in `reviewer-usage.test.ts` and `detect.test.ts`, alongside a late jsdom MutationObserver callback throwing `ReferenceError: Element is not defined` from `activity-motion.ts:58`. The two failing test files passed together when rerun in isolation (26/26), and a separate local UI smoke step passed. I left the unrelated observer lifecycle untouched.

On the second required scoped attempt, the remote build and tests passed, but UI smoke failed because that runner could not reach Google Fonts. The earlier local smoke attempt had timed out while navigating under load; the isolated local smoke retry passed. A third required scoped run completed green on the local fallback: build, format, lint, rendered contrast, the changed-path suite, UI smoke, and the user-docs build all passed. Earlier in implementation, formatting failed once and a prompt assertion needed updating after enumeration wording moved between two phrases; both were corrected, and the focused prompt suite passed.

The control flow spans a server route, a store request, and a dialog in the task drawer. Both client eligibility and server eligibility are enforced because the UI snapshot can become stale between opening the dialog and submitting it. The server is authoritative and reruns the landing checklist at submission time.

On this resumed run, the first required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` completed build and type checking, then reported 7,779 passing tests and one unrelated timeout in `remote-host-pool.test.ts` (`breaks an orphaned lock dir within the wait budget`). The wrapper's strict boot-timing second pass passed. I followed `docs/debugging-check-failures.md` and ran that exact test in isolation with Bun; it passed in 5.98 seconds (1 passed, 164 skipped), so it was not reproducible alone. The relevant runtime versions were Bun 1.4.4 and Node 26.13.1. I reran the required scoped check against the unchanged code tree; it passed, including the selected test suite, rendered contrast audit, UI smoke and user-docs build.

## Key learnings

A mandatory reviewer closing line needs parser support, otherwise output-format compliance can accidentally change the verdict. Stable class history also needs a contract in the prompt; free-form report prose is not a reliable source for cross-pass grouping. Human acceptance should be captured as an auditable reason and enforced again at the server boundary. Finally, a “Land anyway” control can preserve the close-out safety model by overriding only a specific verdict check while requiring all other preflight checks and the normal pipeline to pass.
